All five sit at the delivered frame's own outermost boxes (fx or fy at 0.07/0.93), none reaches a fail bar, and the worst is +0.063 px FWHM / -0.037 roundness — 4x to 5x smaller than the defect being fixed. CORRECTIONS_TO_MY_OWN_EARLIER_CLAIMS_bot.1_set_diversity: I told the owner 'member COUNT does not predict it; SET diversity does'. TOO STRONG. Re-measured with Spearman: at POINT grain members rho=+0.576 vs sets rho=+0.581 (p=0.001 both) — indistinguishable. Only at full-box (350 px) grain do they separate, members +0.329 (p=0.076, not significant) vs sets +0.492 (p=0.006). So set diversity is the better predictor at the grain a measurement box actually uses, and an AGGREGATE marker rather than a per-position rule; the worker's counterexamples stand (midx01 fails losing no set; the x10 band loses 2 sets and passes).
CORRECTIONS_TO_MY_OWN_EARLIER_CLAIMS_bot.2_hix01: my headline +0.343 px is overstated: the arm box CENTRE there is covered by ZERO members (n=17, box offset 1.62 deg) — a coverage straddle. The defect is real; that particular magnitude is not representative. midx02 (+0.230, n=568) is the honest headline.
CORRECTIONS_TO_MY_OWN_EARLIER_CLAIMS_bot.3_the_control_is_not_clean_either: CONFIRMED. The control's own left band reads FWHM 3.28-3.38 and roundness 0.75-0.82 against its interior 2.55-2.59 and 0.94-0.97. 'The original looks fine' is true at the owner's visual threshold, not by the instrument — the crop raised an existing defect above that threshold rather than creating a new class.
